# Step 1: Obtain Initial Metadata from Each Project

To obtain the initial metadata:
1. Search for the BioProject ID (e.g., "PRJEBXXXX") on the [NCBI SRA website](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Traces/study/).
2. In the "Select" table, click on "Metadata" and download the file.
3. The downloaded file is typically named "SraRunTable.csv" and contains metadata for the project.
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)

setwd("C:/Users/zyc/Desktop/oral_project/PRJNA555622")
initial_meta <- read.csv("SraRunTable.csv", header = TRUE) 
head(initial_meta)
```
# Step 2: Create a Uniform Metadata Template

The uniform metadata should include the following columns:

1. **BioProject**: Project ID (e.g., "PRJNA339212")
2. **Run**: Sample ID (e.g., "ERRXXXXXX" or "SRRXXXXXX")
3. **sample_name**: Original sample name submitted by the authors (not the database-assigned ID)
4. **Age**: Age of the subject (if available)
5. **BMI**: Body Mass Index (if available)
6. **Sex**: Sex of the subject ("F" or "M")
7. **Region**: Targeted 16S rRNA region (e.g., "V3-V4")
8. **Platform**: Sequencing platform (e.g., "Illumina MiSeq")
9. **Country**: Country of sample origin (e.g., "China")
10. **Site**: Sample site (e.g., "saliva", "dental plaque")
11. **public_time**: Data release date (format: "YYYY-MM-DD")
12. **PCR_primers**: PCR primers used (e.g., "515F-806R")
13. **title**: Title of the associated publication
14. **Disease_study**: Whether the study involves a disease ("YES" or "NO")
15. **Status**: Disease status (e.g., "T2DM", "HC"). Note: If the study includes both disease and healthy samples, this must be specified per sample.
16. **matched_samples**: matched samples ("YES" or "NO")
```{r}
metadata <- data.frame(
  BioProject = initial_meta$BioProject,
  Run = initial_meta$Run,
  sample_name = initial_meta$Sample.Name,
  Age = NA, 
  BMI = NA,  
  Sex = NA,
  Platform = initial_meta$Instrument,
  # Country = initial_meta$geo_loc_name_country,
  # Status = initial_meta$Host_disease,
  # Site = initial_meta$isolation_source,
  public_time = initial_meta$ReleaseDate,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
```
# Step 3: Manually Add Information from the Publication

Some information (e.g. PCR primers, study title, disease status) must be manually extracted from the publication and added to the metadata.
```{r}

 # metadata <- metadata %>%
 #  mutate(Sex = recode(Sex, "female" = "F", "male" = "M"))
 # metadata <- metadata %>%mutate(Age = Age/12)

```

```{r}
metadata$Country = "America"
metadata$Site = "Supragingival plaques"
metadata$Status = NA
metadata$matched_samples = "NO"
metadata$Region = "V3-V4"
metadata$title <- "Ethnic variation of oral microbiota in children"
metadata$Disease_study <- "NO"
metadata$PCR_primers <- "F:TCGTCGGCAGCGTCAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGCCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG;R:GTCTCGTGGGCTCGGAGATGTGTATAAGAGACAGGACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC"
head(metadata)
```
# Step 4: Summarize and Validate the Metadata
```{r}
print(paste("Number of unique runs:", length(unique(metadata$Run))))
print(paste("Number of unique sample names:", length(unique(metadata$sample_name))))
```
# Step 5: Visualize the Metadata
```{r}
plot_data <- metadata %>%
  select(-BioProject, -Run, -sample_name, -title)

# Function to create simple plots for each column
create_simple_plots <- function(data) {
  plots <- list()
  
  for (col in colnames(data)) {
    # Check if the column is all NA
    if (all(is.na(data[[col]]))) {
      # Create an empty plot with text indicating all NA
      p <- ggplot() +
        annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 0.5, label = "this column is NA", size = 6) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_void()
    } else if (is.numeric(data[[col]])) {
      # Numeric variable: histogram
      p <- ggplot(data, aes(x = .data[[col]])) +
        geom_histogram(fill = "blue", alpha = 0.6, bins = 20, na.rm = T) +
        labs(title = col) +
        theme_minimal()
    } else {
      # Categorical variable: bar plot (remove NA values)
      count_data <- as.data.frame(table(data[[col]], useNA = "ifany"))
      p <- ggplot(count_data, aes(x = reorder(Var1, -Freq), y = Freq)) +
        geom_col(fill = "red", alpha = 0.6) +
        labs(title = col, x = NULL, y = "Count") +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1))
    }
    plots[[col]] <- p
  }
  
  return(plots)
}


plots <- create_simple_plots(plot_data)
p<-plot_grid(plots$Age, 
          plots$BMI, 
          plots$Sex, 
          plots$Region, 
          plots$Platform, 
          plots$Country, 
          plots$Site,
          plots$public_time, 
          # plots$PCR_primers,
          plots$Disease_study,
          plots$Status,
          plots$matched_samples,# add 
          ncol = 3, align = "hv", axis = "lb")
ggsave("Metadata_Summary.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 150)


```

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("Metadata_Summary.png")
```
# Step 6: Finalize and Export the Metadata
```{r}
metadata <- metadata[, c(
  "BioProject", "Run", "sample_name", "Age", "BMI", "Sex", 
  "Region", "Platform", "Country", "Site", "public_time", 
  "PCR_primers", "title", "Disease_study", "Status","matched_samples"
)]

write.csv(metadata, file = "metadata.csv", quote = FALSE)

```
